## Description

Cask `realforce` is stuck at version 4.0.1 while the latest version is 4.1.1.

The livecheck scrapes `https://www.realforce.co.jp/support/download/software/` but the site is behind Cloudflare bot protection, returning 403 for all non-browser requests. This prevents both `brew livecheck` and BrewTestBot autobump from detecting the new version.

The download URL for 4.0.1 has also been removed by the vendor, so the current cask is completely broken — `brew install --cask realforce` fails with a 403 error.

## New version info

- Version: 4.1.1
- URL: `https://www.realforce.co.jp/support/download/software/mac/files/REALFORCE%20CONNECT%20Software_4-1-1.pkg`
- SHA256: `b05654444e7d73b01c8b22e8dbe5b71bf98c8c1a9d0f0122a38134256666de19`

## Steps to reproduce

```
brew livecheck --cask realforce
# Returns no output (Cloudflare blocks the request)

brew install --cask realforce
# Fails with: Download failed: curl: (56) The requested URL returned error: 403
```

### Verification

- [x] I understand that if I ignore these instructions, my issue may be closed without review.
- [x] I have retried my command with `--force`.
- [x] I ran `brew update-reset && brew update` and retried my command.
- [x] I ran `brew doctor`, fixed as many issues as possible and retried my command.
- [x] I have checked the instructions for reporting bugs.
- [x] I made doubly sure this is not a checksum mismatch error.

### Description of issue

Several JetBrains / IntelliJ Platform IDE casks install command-line launchers either through generated shim scripts or by directly linking an app-bundle executable.

The casks install successfully. The issue is the runtime behavior of the installed command-line launchers on macOS: related IDE casks currently use different launcher patterns, and those patterns have different trade-offs for normal GUI/project launches, `--wait`, terminal-oriented commands such as `--help`, `--version`, `format`, `inspect`, and optional wrapper-level aliases such as `-w`.

I checked the cask state at Homebrew/homebrew-cask commit [`8dcf314`](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/commit/8dcf314).

On my system, I have the following affected/related IDE casks installed:

| Installed cask | Launcher type at that commit |
| --- | --- |
| `android-studio` | direct binary |
| `goland` | shim using `open` |
| `intellij-idea` | shim using `open` |
| `phpstorm` | shim direct-exec |
| `pycharm` | shim direct-exec |
| `rustrover` | shim direct-exec |

The part I’m trying to clarify is not whether each individual launcher can start the IDE — they can — but which behavior Homebrew wants to provide consistently for these related casks.

There appear to be three relevant launcher variants.

#### 1. Direct-exec shim scripts

These execute the app bundle binary directly, for example:

```sh
exec "#{appdir}/PhpStorm.app/Contents/MacOS/phpstorm" "$@"
```

This preserves terminal stdout/stderr and exit behavior for terminal-oriented invocations such as `--help`, `--version`, `format`, or `inspect`.

However, normal GUI launch commands like:

```sh
phpstorm .
```

remain attached to the terminal. The IDE window opens successfully, but the shell command does not return, and the terminal receives the IDE process' stdout/stderr output until the IDE exits or the process is interrupted.

This direct-exec behavior also makes wait-style tests hard to interpret: a direct-exec launcher blocks for `--wait <file>`, but it also blocks for ordinary GUI/project opens.

#### 2. `open`-based shim scripts

These use macOS LaunchServices, for example:

```sh
open -na "#{appdir}/GoLand.app" --args "$@"
```

This behaves well for normal GUI/project launches because the shell prompt returns immediately.

However, terminal-style informational options such as:

```sh
goland --help
idea --version
```

do not preserve the IDE launcher stdout/stderr in the terminal.

A plain `open -na ... --args --wait ...` also does not provide shell-level waiting unless `open -W` is used.

#### 3. Direct binary links to app-bundle executables

Some IntelliJ Platform IDE casks do not use a generated shim script but link directly to an executable inside the app bundle, for example:

```ruby
binary "#{appdir}/Android Studio.app/Contents/MacOS/studio"
```

These have behavior similar to direct-exec shim scripts: the IDE opens, but the shell command remains in the foreground and the terminal receives IDE stdout/stderr output until the process exits or is interrupted.

#### JetBrains documented launcher behavior

JetBrains' macOS command-line documentation shows a LaunchServices-style shell launcher. For example, the PhpStorm documentation shows this launcher pattern:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
open -na "PhpStorm.app" --args "$@"
```

The IntelliJ IDEA documentation shows the same pattern for `idea`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
open -na "IntelliJ IDEA.app" --args "$@"
```

The same documentation explains the relevant `open` options:

- `-a` specifies the application
- `-n`
payload.title: JetBrains/IntelliJ Platform IDE launchers have inconsistent macOS CLI behavior

## Problem Summary

After installing `wetype` via Homebrew, the installation appears to succeed — the icon is visible in Launchpad and `/Applications/WeType.app` exists. However:

1. Opening `WeType.app` produces no visible response;
2. WeType does not appear in macOS Input Sources settings;
3. `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/wetype/2.1.0,601/` only contains `WeType.app` — no `WeTypeInstaller_*.app` that older versions used;
4. The cask installs `WeType.app` as a regular app without completing input method registration.

Homebrew reports success, but WeType is effectively unusable as an input method.

**Note:** Previous versions of the `wetype` cask required a manual installation step — after `brew install`, users had to open `WeTypeInstaller_*.app` to register the input method. With `2.1.0,601`, `brew install` completes without error and no longer prompts for this step, which may give users the impression that the installation is fully done. However, the input method is still not registered in macOS.

---

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| Device | Apple Silicon MacBook Air |
| macOS | 26.5 |
| Homebrew prefix | `/opt/homebrew` |
| Cask / Version | `wetype` `2.1.0,601` |

---

## `brew info wetype`

```
==> wetype ✔ (WeType, 微信输入法): 2.1.0,601 (auto_updates)
Text input app from WeChat team for Chinese users
https://z.weixin.qq.com/
Installed (on request)
/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/wetype/2.1.0,601 (570.4MB)
From: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/HEAD/Casks/w/wetype.rb
==> Artifacts
WeType.app (App)
==> Analytics
install: 400 (30 days), 995 (90 days), 2,760 (365 days)
```

Artifact is only `WeType.app (App)` — no installer, no caveats.

---

## `brew cat wetype` — Artifacts

```json
{
  "artifacts": [
    { "app": ["WeType.app"] },
    { "zap": [{ "trash": [
        "~/Library/Application Support/WeType",
        "~/Library/Caches/com.tencent.inputmethod.wetype",
        "~/Library/Caches/WeType",
        "~/Library/HTTPStorages/com.tencent.inputmethod.wetype",
        "~/Library/Preferences/com.tencent.inputmethod.wetype.plist"
    ]}] }
  ],
  "caveats": null
}
```

No installer logic, no postflight registration, no caveat for manual setup.

---

## Input Method Declarations in Info.plist

`plutil -p /Applications/WeType.app/Contents/Info.plist` shows:

| Key | Value |
|-----|-------|
| `TISInputSourceID` | `com.tencent.inputmethod.wetype.pinyin` |
| `InputMethodServerControllerClass` | `WeType.InputController` |
| `InputMethodConnectionName` | `WeType_Connection` |
| `LSUIElement` | `true` |
| `CFBundleIdentifier` | `com.tencent.inputmethod.wetype` |

`WeType.app` declares itself as an input method bundle, but macOS does not register it.

---

## macOS Input Method List — Not Found

```bash
$ defaults read com.apple.HIToolbox AppleEnabledInputSources | grep -Ei 'wetype|tencent'
# (no output)

$ defaults read com.apple.HIToolbox AppleInputSourceHistory | grep -Ei 'wetype|tencent'
# (no output)

$ ls -lah "/Library/Input Methods" "$HOME/Library/Input Methods" | grep -Ei 'WeType|tencent'
# (no output)
```

---

## Code Signing & Gatekeeper: OK

```
$ spctl --assess --type execute --verbose /Applications/WeType.app

source=Notarized Developer ID

$ codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/WeType.app
/Applications/WeType.app: valid on disk
/Applications/WeType.app: satisfies its Designated Requirement
```

Not a signing or Gatekeeper issue.

---

## Actual Behavior

| # | Observation |
|---|-------------|
| 1 | `brew install --cask wetype` succeeds |
| 2 | `/Applications/WeType.app` exists |
| 3 | WeType icon appears in Launchpad |
| 4 | Opening WeType.app produces no visible response |

| 6 | WeType absent from `AppleEnabledInputSources` and `AppleInputSourceHistory` |
| 7 | WeType absent from `/Library/Input Methods` and `~/Library/Input Methods` |
| 8 | No `WeTypeInstaller_*.app` in the current cas

depends_on macos: :monterey

```shell
Error: It seems the App source '/Applications/AltTab.app' is not there.
```

The reason I was trying to uninstall/zap the cask was that AltTab had already started repeatedly surfacing macOS privacy prompts before I deleted the app. After the app was manually deleted, Homebrew still reported `alt-tab` as installed and the normal non-force uninstall path did not clean up the remaining cask/user state. The stale state included:

```shell
/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/alt-tab/7.36.0/AltTab.app
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos.plist
~/Library/Application Support/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos
~/Library/Caches/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos
~/Library/HTTPStorages/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos
~/Library/Preferences/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos.plist
```

`/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/alt-tab/7.36.0/AltTab.app` was a broken symlink/staged app entry pointing at the already deleted `/Applications/AltTab.app`, so there was no runnable app left there to inspect. However, `brew list --cask` still included `alt-tab` until uninstall was retried with `--force`.

The forced uninstall succeeded:

```shell
$ brew uninstall --cask --force alt-tab --zap
==> Dispatching zap stanza
==> Trashing files:
~/Library/Application Support/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos
~/Library/Caches/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos
~/Library/Cookies/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos.binarycookies
~/Library/HTTPStorages/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos
~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos.plist
~/Library/Preferences/com.lwouis.alt-tab-macos.plist
==> Removing all staged versions of Cask 'alt-tab'
```

I think the sharp edge is that the non-force uninstall aborts before running the cleanup/zap work, which leaves a user in a bad state if they manually deleted the app first. It would be much friendlier if `brew uninstall --cask <cask> --zap` still ran uninstall/zap cleanup when the primary app artifact is already missing, or at least printed an explicit suggestion to rerun with `--force --zap`.

## Command that failed

```shell
brew uninstall --cask alt-tab --zap
```

## Output of command with `--verbose --debug`

I no longer have the full `--verbose --debug` output because the affected machine has already been cleaned up and I am avoiding reinstalling AltTab to reproduce the repeated prompt behavior.

The observed failing output from the original command was:

```shell
Error: It seems the App source '/Applications/AltTab.app' is not there.
```

Relevant state observed before forced cleanup:

```shell
$ brew list --cask | rg -i '^alt-tab$'
alt-tab

$ brew info --cask alt-tab
==> alt-tab (AltTab): 10.12.0 (auto_updates)

==> Artifacts
AltTab.app (App)

$ ls -ld /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/alt-tab/7.36.0/AltTab.app

payload.author: frankea
payload.body:
The [`whisky` cask](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/master/Casks/w/whisky.rb) was deprecated on `2025-04-09` because the original [whisky-app/whisky](https://github.com/whisky-app/whisky) repo was archived with a final maintenance notice. The deprecation comment notes:

> As the cask is reasonably popular, disabling could be delayed beyond 12 months from deprecation date, if it is still functional.

That 12-month mark is now (May 2026). I want to flag an active community fork and ask what the project would prefer as the path forward.

## Context

**Active fork:** [frankea/Whisky](https://github.com/frankea/Whisky)

- Continued development through 2026 (latest release `app-v3.0.1`, May 2026)
- Native SwiftUI macOS app, signed and notarized for Apple Silicon (Sequoia 15+)
- Same architecture as upstream (Wine + DXVK + D3DMetal/MoltenVK)
- GPL v3, full source + DocC docs in repo
- Per-issue [audit](https://github.com/frankea/Whisky/blob/main/docs/AUDIT.md) of how the fork addresses the archived upstream's open issues
- Already has a working tap at [frankea/homebrew-whisky](https://github.com/frankea/homebrew-whisky) for users who find it

## What's different from the deprecated cask

- **Bundle identifier changed**: `com.isaacmarovitz.Whisky` → `com.franke.Whisky`. Per cask guidelines this technically makes it a different app, so a straight URL update on the existing cask would be incorrect.
- **Distribution format**: DMG instead of ZIP (signed/notarized via standard `notarytool` workflow).
- **Maintenance**: independent maintainer (not affiliated with original).

## Possible paths and my question

I see three possible paths and want to defer to maintainer preference rather than guess:

1. **Status quo** — let the existing cask reach its disablement date as planned, with users discovering the tap independently. Lowest disruption.
2. **Add a successor cask** like `whisky-fork` (or similar) in homebrew-cask itself, alongside the deprecated `whisky`. Users searching `brew search whisky` would see both, with the deprecated one clearly marked.
3. **Update the deprecation notice** on the existing cask to mention the fork (e.g. via `discontinued! date: …, because: <link to fork>`), which would surface the redirect to anyone running `brew install --cask whisky`.

I'd be happy to do the implementation work for whichever option (if any) the maintainers prefer. Filing this as an issue rather than a PR because the right answer depends on policy I don't want to presume.

Thanks for the time, and for the great work on homebrew-cask in general.
payload.title: whisky: cask is deprecated as :unmaintained — guidance on next step

payload.author: andrewhsu
payload.body:
## Description

The `gcloud-cli` cask symlinks `completion.zsh.inc` into `site-functions` as `_google_cloud_sdk`:

```
/opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_google_cloud_sdk -> /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/gcloud-cli/561.0.0/google-cloud-sdk/completion.zsh.inc
```

However, this file doesn't follow the zsh completion convention that `compinit` expects for files in `site-functions/`. It uses `bashcompinit` and bash-style `complete` commands instead of starting with a `#compdef` header:

```zsh
# What the file has:
autoload -U +X bashcompinit && bashcompinit
...
complete -o nospace -o default -F _python_argcomplete "gcloud"

# What compinit expects for autoloading:
#compdef gcloud bq gsutil
```

For comparison, a properly formatted completion file like `_gh`:
```zsh
#compdef gh
compdef _gh gh
```

## Impact

Running `compinit` finds the file but doesn't know which commands it provides completions for, so `gcloud <Tab>` doesn't work. Users must source the file explicitly as a workaround:

```zsh
source /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_google_cloud_sdk
```

This is the same underlying issue as #143596, which was closed without addressing the convention mismatch.

## Possible fixes

1. Don't symlink `completion.zsh.inc` into `site-functions/` — it's not a `compinit`-compatible file. Instead, document that users should source it directly.
2. Add a thin wrapper in `site-functions/_google_cloud_sdk` that has the proper `#compdef gcloud bq gsutil` header and sources the upstream file.

## Environment

```
macOS, Homebrew, gcloud-cli 561.0.0, zsh 5.9
```
payload.title: gcloud-cli: zsh completion symlink in site-functions doesn't follow #compdef convention

### Description of issue

### Bug Description
Installation of `gcloud-cli` via Cask fails consistently during the `postflight` phase when it attempts to create a virtualenv using the Homebrew-provided Python (e.g., python@3.13 or python@3.14). 

The issue is twofold:
1. Python 3.13/3.14 fails to properly handle the download redirect for the `cryptography` wheel from GitHub to S3, resulting in a 0-byte file. This causes pip to fail with `ERROR: Wheel 'cryptography' ... is invalid.`
2. The cask setup completely strips environment variables, so workarounds like `CLOUDSDK_CORE_DISABLE_VIRTUALENV=1` or `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3` are ignored during `postflight`.

### Steps to reproduce
Run `brew install --cask gcloud-cli` on an Apple Silicon Mac.

It fails with:
Error: Failure while executing; `/usr/bin/env /opt/homebrew/share/google-cloud-sdk/bin/gcloud config virtualenv create --python-to-use /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.13/libexec/bin/python3` exited with 1. Here's the output:
...
Collecting cryptography==42.0.7
  Downloading https://github.com/googleapis/enterprise-certificate-proxy/releases/download/v0.3.6/cryptography-42.0.7-cp39-abi3-macosx_10_12_universal2.whl
     - 0 bytes ? 0:00:00
ERROR: Wheel 'cryptography' located at /private/tmp/.../cryptography-42.0.7-cp39-abi3-macosx_10_12_universal2.whl is invalid.

### The Proof
If you run the exact same `virtualenv create` command manually using the system Python (`/usr/bin/python3`, which is Python 3.9), the download works perfectly (5.6 MB downloaded) and the setup completes without issues.

### Suggested Fix
1. Do not hardcode the dependency on `python@3.1x` if it breaks `gcloud` internal pip downloads, OR
2. Stop filtering out `CLOUDSDK_CORE_DISABLE_VIRTUALENV` and `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON` during the `postflight` step so users can bypass the broken virtualenv creation or specify a working Python binary.

brew install --cask gcloud-cli

### Description of issue

Apologize ahead that this is technically not a bug, but I couldn't find a better way to submit this proposal. Please let me know if there's a right place where this can go.

I install `git` formulae from [homebrew core](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/blob/HEAD/Formula/g/git.rb), and by default it injects a system-wide config at `/opt/homebrew/etc/gitconfig` with content as follow:

```
[credential]
    helper = osxkeychain
```

This instructs Git to use macOS's native keychain for credential storage and access, which aligns with the built-in `git` configuration and is perfectly fine.

However, when I install `git-credential-manager` [cask](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/HEAD/Casks/g/git-credential-manager.rb), it does not modify the config by default, which does not align with what the [official repo's README claims](https://github.com/git-ecosystem/git-credential-manager?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-use).

I think whether a cask should modify the config is up for debate, but I would suggest adding a caveat callout so whoever installs this knows immediately that post-install configuration is required.

I noticed Teams was not on the latest version according to the prompt in-app.

I executed brew bump --open-pr microsoft-teams and found the cask is auto bumped.

I checked the PRs and it appears the last PR by BrewTestBot for this cask was Nov 6, 2025.

I ran brew livecheck --autobump microsoft-teams and was given the following output,
microsoft-teams: 25290.302.4044.3989 ==> 25290.302.4044.3989

I checked the latest release via the URL provided in the .rb comments and found the latest version should be 26032.605.4378.6183. I would expect the livecheck function to return this version, not the old version it is currently returning, therefore the auto bump will not update the cask, despite a new version existing.

[microsoft-teams.rb ln 21](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/6768e174a3454cc9b04f9ebe8e4f896ee89cb488/Casks/m/microsoft-teams.rb):

    strategy :json do |json|
      json.dig("BuildSettings", "WebView2", "macOS", "latestVersion")
    end
  end
```
Perhaps the API in the URL in this livecheck no longer works the way it used to? I am a new contributor and unfamiliar with how this function works, but it appears to me that as the current version number is parsed into the URL, it will simply return the same version.

- [x] I have checked the instructions for [reporting bugs](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask#reporting-bugs).
- [x] I made doubly sure this is not a [checksum does not match / SHA256 mismatch](https://docs.brew.sh/Common-Issues#cask---checksum-does-not-match) error (do not open an issue before trying to open a PR to fix first).

### Description of issue

Environment:
- macOS 26.3
- Obsidian 1.12.4
- Homebrew installed via API (cask revision containing the binary artifact)

The current obsidian cask exposes the internal executable as a binary:
```shell
/opt/homebrew/bin/obsidian -> /Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/MacOS/Obsidian
```

Launching Obsidian through this shim causes Electron to crash with repeated:
```shell
FATAL:electron/shell/app/electron_main_delegate_mac.mm:65] Unable to find helper app
```
followed by:
```shell
FATAL:content/browser/gpu/gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

#### Reproduction

```shell
brew install --cask obsidian
obsidian
```

Result: crash with helper lookup errors.

However launching the executable directly works:
```shell
/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/MacOS/obsidian
```

#### Workaround

Removing the Homebrew shim resolves the issue:
```shell
rm /opt/homebrew/bin/obsidian
```

After removing it, the shell resolves `obsidian` directly to the bundle binary and the application launches normally.

#### Additional notes

Both
```shell
/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/MacOS/Obsidian
/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/MacOS/obsidian
```
exist and are identical binaries (same SHA256). The issue appears to stem from Electron helper resolution when launched via the Homebrew shim.

It may be safer for the cask to avoid exposing the internal executable as a binary artifact.

This started after the cask began installing a CLI shim via the binary stanza ([commit “obsidian: add binary stanza for CLI”]( https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/commit/a38786dd6e90470ffe6103e7f9eca29870980981)), i.e.:
```ruby
binary "#{appdir}/Obsidian.app/Contents/MacOS/Obsidian", target: "obsidian"
```
which creates `/opt/homebrew/bin/obsidian -> .../Contents/MacOS/Obsidian`.

When launching Electron apps via an alternate executable name/path, Electron may fail to locate the “Helper.app” bundles and crash with “Unable to find helper app”. This matches the known Electron/electron-builder failure mode when the app/binary naming diverges ([“Unable to find helper app” at startup](https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/6962)).

Removing the Homebrew shim (`rm /opt/homebrew/bin/obsidian`) makes the shell resolve to the bundle executable directly and avoids the crash.

#### Potential fix

Drop the binary stanza (or switch it to a wrapper that uses `open -a "Obsidian" --args ...` instead of linking to the inner Mach-O).

```shel

```

payload.body:
## Describe the bug

When running `brew upgrade --cask codex`, Homebrew reports the latest version is already installed. However, the Codex app itself shows an in-app update prompt indicating a newer version is available.

## To Reproduce

1. Install Codex via Homebrew: `brew install --cask codex`
2. 2. Run `brew upgrade --cask codex`
3. 3. Homebrew outputs: `Warning: Not upgrading codex, the latest version is already installed`
4. 4. Launch the Codex app → app shows an update notification/prompt
## Expected behavior

The Homebrew Cask formula version should stay in sync with the latest version distributed by OpenAI, so that `brew upgrade --cask codex` actually upgrades the app when a new version is available.

## Environment

- macOS: 15.7.4 (Sequoia, Build: 24G517)
- - Homebrew: 5.0.16
- - - Codex version (installed via Cask): 26.228.1430
## Possible cause

The Homebrew Cask formula version may not be updated promptly after each Codex release, causing a version mismatch between the Cask registry and the app's internal update checker.

payload.body:
## Bug Report

**Cask:** android-sdk
**Command:** `brew uninstall --cask android-sdk`
**Exit code:** 1

### Description

Running `brew uninstall --cask android-sdk` fails with the error:

```
Error: Unexpected method 'discontinued' called during caveats on Cask android-sdk.
```

The cask has both `disable! date: "2024-12-16", because: :discontinued` and a `caveats` block containing `depends_on_java "8"`. It appears that evaluating the caveats block during uninstall incorrectly triggers the `:discontinued` symbol as a method call in the caveats context.

This makes it impossible to uninstall the cask via `brew uninstall`.

### Cask Definition

```ruby
cask "android-sdk" do
  version "4333796"
  # ...
  disable! date: "2024-12-16", because: :discontinued

  # ...

  caveats do
    depends_on_java "8"
  end
end
```

### Description of issue

The cask intellij-idea-ce is marked as deprecated because it's "discontinued upstream", and the cask source links to https://blog.jetbrains.com/idea/2025/12/intellij-idea-unified-release/.

However, the open-source part of IntelliJ IDEA (as well as other IDEs based on the IntelliJ platform) will still be distributed via releases in the GitHub repository. More details here: https://lp.jetbrains.com/intellij-idea-unified-faq/

The difference between the unified release (available as cask intellij-idea) with a free license and the open-source build is the latter has no AI features, settings sync, automatic updates and closed-source plugins included in main product. The former contains only the fully open-source functionalities, with an Apache 2.0 license.

It is still called "intellij-community" as far as I know, since the repo keeps this name, thus I see no need for renaming the cask.

I believe we should not mark this cask as deprecated in such case, instead updating it to point to GitHub releases and not using auto_updates (since they won't be available for the open-source builds). By doing that, we'll keep offering the open-source variant for users that could install the "complete" free version (open-source components + closed-source features + auto updates) but prefer using a fully free option.

payload.body:
## Description

[HP Display Center](https://support.hp.com/us-en/drivers/hp-z27xs-g3-4k-usb-c-dreamcolor-display/2100175425) is HP's official macOS application for color calibration and display configuration of HP DreamColor and business monitors.

It is not currently available via Homebrew, nor has it ever been proposed (searched issues/PRs — zero results).

> **Note:** HP Display Center ≠ HP Display Manager. Display Manager is a Windows-only IT admin tool [being deprecated](https://ftp.hp.com/pub/caps-softpaq/cmit/displays/HP_DisplayManager.html) in favor of HP CMSL. Display Center is the end-user calibration app (this request).

## Package details

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| **Name** | HP Display Center |
| **Bundle ID** | `com.HP.HPDC` |
| **Version** | 2.5.3 (build 5) |
| **Min macOS** | 12.0 (Monterey) via `LSMinimumSystemVersion` |
| **Architecture** | Universal (x86_64 + arm64) |
| **Signed by** | HP Inc. (`6HB5Y2QTA3`), Apple Developer ID |
| **Built with** | Xcode 16.2, macOS SDK 15.2 |
| **Download URL** | `https://ftp.hp.com/pub/softpaq/sp165501-166000/hpdc-mac.tar` |
| **SHA256 (tar)** | `135768fd0f2dad7d9f6263843aeb5ebef6b7d317a8b5621a0160cf41770c8191` |
| **Format** | `.tar` containing `HPDC-Mac.pkg` |
| **Size** | ~34.6 MB |
| **Homepage** | https://support.hp.com/ |

## Installed artifacts (from BOM)

- `/Applications/HPDC-Mac.app` — main application (597 files)
- `/Library/Scripts/HPDC/HPDC_scheduler_run` — scheduler helper binary (arm64-only)

## Bundled frameworks

- `HPDC_Calibration.framework` (includes i1d3SDK, i1Pro, i1Pro3, NSKClmtr for colorimeter support)
- `HPDC_Camera.framework`
- `HPDC_Display.framework`
- `HPDC_Scheduler.framework`
- `HPDC_ScreenPartition.framework`

## Localizations

en, de, es, fr, it, ja, nl, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant

## Notes

- **No LaunchDaemons/Agents** — no background services, clean uninstall.
- **Preinstall script** only cleans old logs/prefs — no interactive UI, safe for silent `installer -pkg`.
- **`pkgutil:` is sufficient for uninstall** — the BOM tracks all installed files (`/Applications/HPDC-Mac.app` and `/Library/Scripts/HPDC/`), so Homebrew's pkgutil stanza handles full cleanup. No explicit `delete:` needed.
- **Real `sha256` is appropriate** — the URL is version-specific (softpaq range `sp165501-166000`); probing other ranges returns 404. When HP releases a new version, the URL will change.

## Livecheck

HP's support page is JS-rendered, but the underlying API can be queried with a `POST` request. Homebrew's `post_json` + `strategy :json` supports this pattern natively.

The minimum viable API call (reverse-engineered from the browser):

```bash
curl -s 'https://support.hp.com/wcc-services/swd-v2/driverDetails' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' \
  -d '{"lc":"en","cc":"us","osTMSId":"18015185915131310124113888731054140111953115","osName":"Mac OS","productSeriesOid":2100175425}'
```

The response contains all historical versions with download URLs. The latest is at `data.softwareTypes[0].softwareDriversList[0].latestVersionDriver`.

**Autobump limitation:** the download URL changes between versions (different softpaq range, e.g. `sp165501-166000` → `sp163001-163500`) and the filename format is inconsistent across versions (`.tar` vs `.dmg`, with and without version in filename). The URL cannot be interpolated from the version string, so automatic PR generation via `brew bump-cask-pr` won't work. Livecheck will detect version changes, but URL + sha256 updates require a manual PR. The cask should include `no_autobump!`.

## Suggested cask

```ruby
cask "hp-display-center" do
  version "2.5.3"
  sha256 "135768fd0f2dad7d9f6263843aeb5ebef6b7d317a8b5621a0160cf41770c8191"

  url "https://ftp.hp.com/pub/softpaq/sp165501-166000/hpdc-mac.tar"
  name "HP Display Center"
  desc "Color calibration and display settings for HP monitors"
  homepage "https://support.hp.com/"

  livecheck do
    url "https://support.hp.

payload.author: MichaelRWolf
payload.body:
Summary
- Installing Homebrew cask cursor-cli results in a quarantined bundled Node binary.
- On Intel macOS, running cursor-agent triggers a Gatekeeper “node” malware warning dialog.
- After clicking “Done”, the process is terminated (Killed: 9).
- Removing the quarantine attribute from the dist-package fixes it immediately.

Environment
- macOS: darwin 24.6.0 (macOS 15.6.x)
- CPU arch: x86_64 (Intel)
- Homebrew cask cursor-cli version: 2026.01.23-916f423
- cursor-agent location:
  /usr/local/bin/cursor-agent -> /usr/local/Caskroom/cursor-cli/2026.01.23-916f423/dist-package/cursor-agent

Repro steps
1) Install:
   brew install --cask cursor-cli
2) Run:
   cursor-agent --version

Actual result
- macOS dialog appears:
  “node” Not Opened
  Apple could not verify “node” is free of malware...
- Terminal shows:
  Killed: 9                  cursor-agent --version

Diagnostics
- The wrapper executes bundled node:
  /usr/local/Caskroom/cursor-cli/2026.01.23-916f423/dist-package/node
- The node binary is x86_64:
  file .../dist-package/node
  -> Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64
- Quarantine attribute is present:
  xattr -l .../dist-package/node
  com.apple.quarantine: 0381;...

- codesign is OK:
  codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=4 .../dist-package/node
  ...: valid on disk
  ...: satisfies its Designated Requirement

- spctl rejects it because it is quarantined and “not an app”:
  spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=4 .../dist-package/node
  ...: rejected (the code is valid but does not seem to be an app)

Expected result
- cursor-agent should run without Gatekeeper prompts or termination.

Workaround / Fix
- Remove quarantine from the dist-package:
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/Caskroom/cursor-cli/2026.01.23-916f423/dist-package
- After that:
  cursor-agent --version
  -> 2026.01.23-916f423

Notes
- This looks like the cask install is preserving quarantine on the downloaded artifact, and the dist-package contains a standalone executable that Gatekeeper blocks when quarantined.
payload.title: cursor-cli: bundled node quarantined; macOS blocks and kills cursor-agent

### Description of issue

The cask `google-chat` should be deleted because the application no longer works. It depends on server-side support that no longer exists. The application has been discontinued upstream.

Brew happily installs it. There is no failure of a `brew` command.

**(1) It depends on server-side support that is no longer offered**

After installing and launching, it prompts you to log in via a web browser. Doing so leads to a Google error page saying:

> This app is blocked
>
> This app tried to access sensitive info in your Google Account. To keep your account safe, Google blocked this access.

I verified this result using both a personal Google account and a Google Workspace (business) account.

Google said they stopped allowing the Electron app in 2021 (source: https://web.archive.org/web/20210319003611/https://support.google.com/chat/answer/10194711). Cash `google-chat-electron` was removed already. Evidently the native version was also shut off.

**(2) The app itself has been discontinued upstream**

Replacement is a "Chrome app" (PWA). (Source: https://support.google.com/chat/answer/9455386?hl=en) which AFAIK out-of-scope for Homebrew. 

The native macOS app download link was removed from the web in September 2020 - compare these (may require Mac browser user agent):
- https://web.archive.org/web/20200916201230/https://chat.google.com/download/
- https://web.archive.org/web/20200923230247/https://chat.google.com/download/

### Description of issue

The current fiji cask appears to default to the Intel (x86_64) build, which triggers a Rosetta 2 installation requirement on Apple Silicon Macs.
However, the upstream provider Fiji offers a native macos Apple Silicon build that includes an ARM64 Java Runtime Environment (JRE). 

As Fiji is a scientific tool used for processing and analysing microscopic images, including large files in batches, running it natively rather than
via Rosetta 2 would confer a significant advantage. I request that the cask be updated accordingly.

Fiji currently lists the ARM64 build under the latest directory rather than stable. While I understand the preference for stable URLs, the performance difference on Apple Silicon is significant enough that a versioned or 'latest' option for ARM64 would be highly beneficial for the scientific community

Technical Reference for Fix:

New ARM64 URL: https://downloads.imagej.net/fiji/latest/fiji-latest-macos-arm64-jdk.zip

payload.body:
Jetbrains [documentation](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ruby/working-with-the-ide-features-from-command-line.html#standalone) recommends:
```shell
#!/bin/sh

open -na "RubyMine.app" --args "$@"
```

This is significantly different from the script created by the RubyMine cask:
https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/2cf14fac0b3781625ecf908419fd761caf8ba2bb/Casks/r/rubymine.rb#L31-L38

The file generated by the JetBrains Toolbox is similar:
```shell
#!/bin/bash
#Generated by JetBrains Toolbox 3.2.0.65851 at 2025-12-18T07:53:50

declare -a intellij_args=()
declare -- wait=""

for o in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$o" = "--wait" || "$o" = "-w" ]]; then
    wait="-W"
    o="--wait"
  fi
  if [[ "$o" =~ " " ]]; then
    intellij_args+=("\"$o\"")
  else
    intellij_args+=("$o")
  fi
done

open -na "/Users/aramprice/Applications/RubyMine.app/Contents/MacOS/rubymine" $wait --args "${intellij_args[@]}"%
```

### Description of issue

dotnet-sdk cask https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/main/Casks/d/dotnet-sdk.rb has this section

```yaml
conflicts_with cask: [
    "dotnet-runtime",
    "dotnet-runtime@preview",
    "dotnet-sdk@8",
    "dotnet-sdk@preview",
  ]
```

I believe this is wrong. Different versions of .NET runtimes and SDKs can live side-by-side perfectly fine.

Proof when installed manually:

```bash
$ dotnet --list-runtimes
Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 8.0.21 [/usr/local/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
Microsoft.AspNetCore.App 10.0.0 [/usr/local/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App]
Microsoft.NETCore.App 8.0.21 [/usr/local/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App]
Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.0 [/usr/local/share/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App]
```

I suggest you remove this line `"dotnet-sdk@8",`

Especially because for some reaosn you allow side-by-side with .NET 9, but not NET 8  😂😂😂😂  I suspect the yaml was updated today because of the .NET 10 release but you forgot to edit all the rest

payload.author: ruff3d
payload.body:
**Bug Description:**
The LibreOffice cask downloads the Intel x86_64 version instead of ARM64 on M1 Macs because `Hardware::CPU.arm?` returns false.

**Expected Behavior:**
On M1 Macs, the cask should download the ARM64 (aarch64) version of LibreOffice.

**Actual Behavior:**
The cask downloads the Intel version because the architecture detection fails.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Run `brew install --cask libreoffice` on an M1 Mac
2. The formula uses `arch arm: "aarch64", intel: "x86-64"`
3. `Hardware::CPU.arm?` returns false on M1, defaulting to Intel
4. Wrong DMG file is downloaded

**System Info:**
- macOS on Apple Silicon (M1)
- `uname -m` returns `arm64`
- `brew ruby -e "puts Hardware::CPU.arm?"` returns `false`

**Suggested Fix:**
Use `Hardware::CPU.physical_cpu_arm64?` instead of `Hardware::CPU.arm?` for proper M1 detection.
payload.title: LibreOffice cask downloads wrong architecture on M1 Macs - Hardware::CPU.arm? returns false

### Description of issue

When trying to upgrade the `cursor` cask via Homebrew, the installation fails with a SHA mismatch. On investigation, it seems the root cause is that the Brew bot created a PR to update `cursor` to `1.6.x`. However, this version has not been officially released by Cursor and is still in **pre-release**.

* Cask file: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/main/Casks/c/cursor.rb
* Cursor changelog: https://cursor.com/changelog (only `1.5.x` is officially released, `1.6.x` is still pre-release)
* Discussion from Cursor community forum: https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-v1-6-pre-release-discussion/133043

**Why this is a problem:**

* The SHA mismatch is a symptom of the deeper issue: the bot is pulling in pre-release versions that should not be distributed to Homebrew users.
* According to https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/HEAD/doc/faq/closing_issues_without_review.md, a SHA mismatch alone is normally closed without review. However, in this case the issue is not just the checksum, it’s that the Brew bot is tracking a pre-release as if it were a stable release.

**Expected behavior:**

* The Brew bot should only create PRs for official stable releases of `cursor`, not pre-releases.

**Actual behavior:**

* Brew bot created PRs for `cursor 1.6.x` which is still in pre-release.
  * https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/pull/227669
  * https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/pull/227518
* Users attempting to install or upgrade get a SHA mismatch error.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Run `brew upgrade --greedy cursor`
2. Observe that it attempts to fetch `1.6.x`
3. Installation fails with SHA mismatch

brew upgrade --greedy cursor

## Bug Report

### Description
When running `brew cleanup` or `brew info --cask adoptopenjdk8`, I encounter the following error:

```
Error: Unexpected method 'appcast' called on Cask adoptopenjdk8.
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Have the `adoptopenjdk/openjdk` tap installed
2. Run `brew cleanup` or `brew info --cask adoptopenjdk8`
3. Error appears consistently

### System Information
- **Homebrew Version**: 4.6.10
- **macOS Version**: 15.6.1
- **Architecture**: x86_64
- **Tap**: adoptopenjdk/openjdk (archived repository)
- **Cask**: adoptopenjdk8

### Additional Context
The cask comes from the `adoptopenjdk/openjdk` tap, but that repository appears to be archived and read-only, so I cannot report the issue there directly. The error suggests there's an issue with the cask definition where an `appcast` method is being called inappropriately.

The cask is located at:
https://github.com/adoptopenjdk/homebrew-openjdk/blob/HEAD/Casks/adoptopenjdk8.rb

Since the tap is archived, users may be stuck with this error. This might warrant either:
1. A fix in Homebrew core to handle the deprecated `appcast` method more gracefully
2. Guidance on how to handle casks from archived taps
3. Migration advice for users affected by this issue

### Expected Behavior
The cask should work without throwing this error during cleanup operations or when querying cask information, or at minimum, provide clear guidance on how to resolve the issue.

### Actual Behavior
The `appcast` method error is thrown, but the operation partially continues (in the case of cleanup, it still removes some files and frees disk space).

### Full Error Output
```

I have managed to temporarily work around the issue by setting the HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1 env variable, but the expected behaviour would be that when passed a path to a cask file, brew is smart enough to interpret it as such and use that instead of interpreting it as a cask name.

Hello! There seems to be a problem when installing Agisoft Metashape through Homebrew. 

The command I'm using is the basic install command:

`brew install --cask metashape`

The problem persists even if I omit the --cask argument:

`brew install metashape`

I have gone through the steps in the "Common Issues - Checksum doesn't match" section of the documentation, and have deleted and re-downloaded the file that Homebrew downloaded (from ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/) a few times.

Furthermore, I have downloaded the file from the vendor's website and compared the SHA256 checksum of that file with the one Homebrew downloads, and they both have the same checksum. This implies that homebrew is downloading the correct file. The signing information on both files are same and both carry a valid and notarised Apple signature. It seems that the file Homebrew downloads is indeed the current version, i.e. 'metashape_2_2_1.dmg" and is identical to the one from the vendor's website. 

Maybe the checksum value in homebrew's list of casks is outdated/wrong?

Happens only in Metashape for me.

(P.S. I downloaded the previous version of Metashape (metashape_2_1_4.dmg) and the checksum does not match the one brew shows as "expected" for the current version, so it does not seem to be the case that Homebrew is trying to match the new version's checksum to the old version either.)

Error: next: It seems the App source '/Applications/Next.app' is not there.
\`\`\`

### System Information
- **Homebrew Version**: 4.5.9
- **macOS Version**: 15.5 (24F74)
- **Cask**: next (version 1.2.0 -> 2.052)

### Additional Context
- The cask appears to be marked as discontinued: \`Disabled because it is discontinued upstream! It was disabled on 2024-12-16.\`
- The error occurs when the \`discontinued\` method is called during caveats processing
- This suggests the cask definition may be using an unsupported method for handling discontinued software

### Expected Behavior
The cask should either:
1. Handle the discontinued state gracefully without throwing an error
2. Be removed from the system if it's truly discontinued
3. Provide a clear message about its discontinued status without breaking the upgrade process

### Reproduction Steps
1. Have the \`next\` cask installed (version 1.2.0)
2. Run \`brew upgrade\`
3. Error occurs when trying to upgrade the next cask

You can find this URL at the [bottom of the vendor page](https://www.bzgapps.com/unite) Here's the "Expected" SHA, which does not match the [committed sha256](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/1c1a9a5ef325059ead38058f3af19d7223021b7a/Casks/u/unite.rb#L3) (notice there's no version) ``` wget -q https://bzgdownloads.s3.amazonaws.com/Unite/Unite.zip && sha256 Unite.zip SHA256 (Unite.zip) = 1229573061e51a1c70f1ee6983688b3b4445196275e2f5449e56d68a14b1b775 ``` ...and this is the correct url to download this `6.3.0.1` release version, which matches the "Actual" by `brew install unite` (above): ``` wget -q https://bzgdownloads.s3.amazonaws.com/Unite/Unite+6.3.0.1.zip && sha256 Unite+6.3.0.1.zip SHA256 (Unite+6.3.0.1.zip) = 4924b23e4a7cc5f85258d3a503fcc2734f3d0ea68f69651393c9945a9764acf2 ``` # Current details ``` brew info unite ==> unite: 6.3.0.1 (auto_updates) https://bzgapps.com/unite Not installed From: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/HEAD/Casks/u/unite.rb ==> Name Unite ==> Description Turn websites into apps ==> Artifacts Unite.app (App) ``` # Note I read through the docs and do not believe this type of issue has a formal/automated solution already implemented, so i'm manually submitting this issue. Where i'm unsure as to how BrewTestBot picked up the incorrect sha256... I'm also happy to manually submit a PR with the required value update so long as it's following the guidelines and will be approved. fwiw, i did reproduce this on another Mac, and also did check the last couple version updates and confirmed the values matched their corresponding downloads. e.g. [Unite 6.3](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/blob/7b46704a46fc8e14e81a888417248eb75b8f1da6/Casks/u/unite.rb): ``` wget -q https://bzgdownloads.s3.amazonaws.com/Unite/Unite+6.3.zip && sha256 Unite+6.3.zip SHA256 (Unite+6.3.zip) = 018fa042c226169ba9786713466b89d1ede0f3a89bee9bdaba5e45d2abef0124 ``` ### Command that failed brew install unite ### Output of command with `--verbose --debug` ```shell ==> Downloading https://formulae.brew.sh/api/formula.jws.json /usr/bin/env /opt/homebrew/Library/Homebrew/shims/shared/curl --disable --cookie /dev/null --globoff --user-agent Homebrew/4.5.6-14-g11f4d30\ \(Macintosh\;\ arm64\ Mac\ OS\ X\ 15.5\)\ curl/8.7.1 --header Accept-Language:\ en --fail --remote-time --output

payload.author: almostturingcomplete
payload.body:
All Objective-See casks that serve prebuilt binaries (.zip) from Bitbucket are currently broken.

This affects multiple casks (reikey, ransomwhere, etc.), as upstream URLs now return HTML pages (likely a Bitbucket access change or removal), instead of valid .zip binaries, leading to SHA256 mismatches and install failures.

These casks use the following pattern:
```
url "https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/<AppName>_<version>.zip",
     verified: "bitbucket.org/objective-see/"
```

Download endpoint [`https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/`](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/) shows no available downloads.

**Affected Casks:**
| Cask | URL | Content-Type
|------|-----|---------------
| `reikey` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/ReiKey_1.4.2.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/ReiKey_1.4.2.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8
| `ransomwhere` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/RansomWhere_1.2.5.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/RansomWhere_1.2.5.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8
| `taskexplorer` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/TaskExplorer_2.0.2.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/TaskExplorer_2.0.2.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8
| `filemonitor` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/FileMonitor_1.3.0.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/FileMonitor_1.3.0.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8
| `lockdown` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/Lockdown_1.0.0.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/Lockdown_1.0.0.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8
| `processmonitor` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/ProcessMonitor_1.5.0.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/ProcessMonitor_1.5.0.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8
| `do-not-disturb` | [https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/DoNotDisturb_1.3.0.zip](https://bitbucket.org/objective-see/deploy/downloads/DoNotDisturb_1.3.0.zip) | text/html; charset=utf-8

> _Script used to generate table:_
> ```
> for cask in reikey ransomwhere taskexplorer filemonitor lockdown processmonitor do-not-disturb; do
>   url=$(brew info --cask --json=v2 "$cask" | jq -r '.casks[].url')
>   content_type=$(curl -sI -L "$url" | ggrep -Po '(?<=^content-type: ).*' | tail -n 1)
>   echo "| \`$cask\` | [$url]($url) | $content_type |"
> done
> ```

**Additionally:**
- These tools appear unmaintained, e.g. the [ReiKey repository’s](https://github.com/objective-see/ReiKey) last commit was 5 years ago
- And these tools are Intel-only (require Rosetta 2 for Apple Silicon)

**Proposal:**
- Should a PR be added with commits to mark all these casks as disabled with reason "unavailable upstream"?

### Description of issue

I'd like to re-raise  #49127 and other tickets filed for this. I believe the original justification given doesn't address the problems that pinning would solve. Therefore, the topic requires a reconsideration.

> @vitorgalvao
>
> A huge chunk of casks auto-update and we can’t stop that. So pin would at best be inconsistent and not work in a lot of cases.
>
> If you do a search you’ll see we’ve discussed this in the past, especially in the upgrade issues on brew’s repository.


### Argument 1: a counter-argument to "pin would at best be inconsistent and not work in a lot of cases"

Casks with `auto_updates` are *effectively* pinned. `brew upgrade` will not update them, unless `--greedy-auto-updates` is passed. They *may* be upgraded externally by the application itself, and Homebrew won't know the actual version installed over time or what files were modified...

...so how is this different from an explicit pin on the package? `auto_updates` and `latest` markers *are* pins. Permanent ones that prevent them from being upgraded on `brew upgrade` - but still pins. They just can't be arbitrarily removed or added by the user to achieve their own goals.


### Argument 2: auto-update feature is often optional, let brew do it

Out of all my `auto_updates` casks listed with `brew info --json=v2 --installed --casks | jq -r '.casks[] | select(.auto_updates) | .token'`, most have optional auto-updates:

- Check optional: iterm2, menumeters, nextcloud, orbstack, teamviewer, visual-studio-code, vlc, wireshark, witch
- Check mandatory but update optional: firefox, imageoptim, macfuse, pika, sublime-text, xee, spectacle
- Check and update mandatory: adobe-acrobat-reader, discord, dropbox, google-chrome, onedrive, signal

How do I update all packages except these listed in "Check and update mandatory" category, without this kind of trickery? `brew upgrade --cask --greedy-auto-updates $(brew info --json=v2 --installed --casks | jq -r '.casks[] | select(.auto_updates) | .token' | grep -vE '^(adobe-acrobat-reader|discord|dropbox|onedrive|signal)$')`

There is absolutely nothing wrong about `brew pin adobe-acrobat-reader discord dropbox google-chrome onedrive signal` so we can `brew update --greedy-auto-updates` and get everything up-to-date except the ones we pinned.


### Argument 3: the fundamental issue

All package manager in existence - except pkgin/pksrc and Homebrew (for casks) - allow their users to "upgrade all except these":

- `pacman -Syu --ignore <pkg1>,<pkg2>`
- `apt-mark hold <pkg1> <pkg2>; apt upgrade; apt-mark unhold <pkg1> <pkg2>`
- `dnf upgrade --refresh --exclude=<pkg1>,<pkg2>`
  - or `dnf versionlock add <pkg1> <pkg2>; dnf upgrade --refresh; dnf versionlock delete <pkg1> <pkg2>`
- `yum update --exclude=<pkg1>,<pkg2>`
  - or `yum versionlock add <pkg1>-* <pkg2>-*; yum update; yum versionlock delete <pkg1>-* <pkg2>-*`
- `zypper up --exclude <pkg1>,<pkg2>`
  - or `zypper addlock <pkg>; zypper up; zypper removelock <pkg>`
- `emerge -avuD --exclude <pkg1>,<pkg2> @world`
  - or add `=<pkg>-*` to `/etc/portage/package.mask`
- `choco upgrade all --except=<pkg1>,<pkg2>`
  - or `choco pin add -n=<pkg>; choco upgrade all; choco pin remove -n=<pkg>`
- `winget pin add --id <P

While trying to setup a MacOS install for flutter with Ansible, I naturally thought I would make it install **both** the `dart-sdk` formula and the `flutter` cask to make sure everything is properly installed (It turns out `flutter` already ships the dart SDK).

Surprisingly, when you try to run `brew install --cask flutter` **after** having installed dart via `brew install dart-sdk`, you get an error:

I do understand that there already is a dart install at /opt/homebrew/bin/dart, that's kind of the whole point of already having it installed, but I don't understand why that would cause an error.

### Feature Request: New Cask for CafeTran

**Issue Type:** Feature Request

**Cask Name:** cafetran

**Description:** CafeTran Espresso is a powerful, feature-rich translation memory tool designed for freelance translators and language service providers. It supports numerous file formats, integrates with machine translation engines, and offers advanced features for terminology management and quality assurance. It is cross-platform, running natively on macOS, Windows, and Linux without requiring special setups.

**Download URLs:**

* **macOS:** [https://www.cafetran.com/download-for-mac/](https://www.cafetran.com/download-for-mac/)
    * **Direct Download Link for Intel Macs:** [https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTranMac-install.dmg](https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTranMac-install.dmg)
    * **Direct Download Link for Apple Silicon (M-series) Macs:** [https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTranMac-arm-install.dmg](https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTranMac-arm-install.dmg)
* **Windows:** [https://www.cafetran.com/download-for-windows-pc/](https://www.cafetran.com/download-for-windows-pc/)
    * **Direct Download Link:** [https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTran-install.exe](https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTran-install.exe)
* **Linux:** [https://www.cafetran.com/download-for-linux/](https://www.cafetran.com/download-for-linux/)
    * **Direct Download Link (.jar file - requires Java):** [https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTran.jar](https://www.cafetran.com/download/CafeTran.jar)

**Homepage:** [https://www.cafetran.com/](https://www.cafetran.com/)

**Rationale:** CafeTran Espresso is a widely used professional translation tool popular across different operating systems due to its native support. It is the best alternative to RWE Trados (formerly SDL Trados), which historically only runs on Windows. Providing a Homebrew Cask would greatly simplify its installation and management for translators already using the Homebrew ecosystem. 

**Additional Notes:** The application offers a fully functional free version with limitations on translation memory and glossary size, allowing users to evaluate it before purchasing a license.

### Description of issue

The `font-plemol-jp` cask in version 2.0.3 does not include `"PlemolJP-Italic.ttf"` in its installation list, even though this font file exists in the official distribution ZIP from upstream.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the cask:

```bash
brew install --cask font-plemol-jp
```

2. Check installed fonts in `~/Library/Fonts`:
`PlemolJP-Regular.ttf` exists, but `PlemolJP-Italic.ttf` is missing.

3. Download the source ZIP:
URL: `https://github.com/yuru7/PlemolJP/releases/download/v2.0.3/PlemolJP_v2.0.3.zip`

4. Verify `PlemolJP/PlemolJP-Italic.ttf` exists in the ZIP.

### Expected behavior
`PlemolJP-Italic.ttf` should be installed along with other fonts like `PlemolJP-Regular.ttf` and `PlemolJPConsole-Italic.ttf`, making 16 fonts for `PlemolJP`.

### Actual behavior
`PlemolJP-Italic.ttf` is not installed, resulting in only 15 fonts for `PlemolJP`.

### Suggested fix
Add the following line to `Casks/font/font-p/font-plemol-jp.rb`:
```ruby
font "PlemolJP_v#{version}/PlemolJP/PlemolJP-Italic.ttf"
```
### Additional context

- The upstream ZIP contains 16 fonts per variant (e.g., `PlemolJPConsole`, `PlemolJP35`), but `font-plemol-jp.rb` omits `PlemolJP-Italic.ttf` for `PlemolJP`.
- This is a cask definition issue, not an upstream problem.

### Description of issue

After installing and then uninstalling `jump-desktop-connect`, it left two processes running:

```
_coreaudiod      33419   0.0  0.0 410331296   5968   ??  Ss    2:53PM   0:00.10 Core Audio Driver (JumpAudioMic.driver)
_coreaudiod      33415   0.0  0.0 410322080   5856   ??  Ss    2:53PM   0:00.11 Core Audio Driver (JumpAudio.driver)
```

The uninstall process did remove the drivers from `/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL/`, but I guess coreaudio needs to be restarted to fully unload them. It looks like the old way of doing this was with `sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.apple.audio.coreaudiod`. However this is no longer permitted. This page: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/macos-release-notes/macos-14_4-release-notes#Core-Audio says:

> To improve security and stability, using launchctl kickstart -k is no longer permitted for critical system processes. If a process must be forcefully terminated, it is recommended to use kill instead.

I was able to accomplish this with:

```
sudo launchctl list | awk '$3=="com.apple.audio.coreaudiod" { system("sudo kill " $1) }'
```

I'm not sure the exact right way to do it via homebrew formula.

payload.author: Oski130
payload.body:
> Essentially, casks with `version` set and `sha256 :no_check` aren't being upgraded if a) the full version number isn't in the URL, and b) the server [doesn't provide a "Last-Modified" header](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/3b52a460593fb3f36e5b5fa4bb541ccbb84a4b79/Library/Homebrew/download_strategy.rb#L422). 
> 
> A simulation: on my machine, with `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1`, using the `captin` cask:
> 
> 1. download v1.3 to the cached path
> ```
> $ curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cool8jay/public/master/captin/Captin1.3.zip -o `brew --cache captin`
> 
> $ find ~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads  -name "*Captin*"
> /Users/eric/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/39266fc3264702ef6586dbeab1060e2a56b6e2d04cab21a136446e5c16446068--Captin.zip
> ```
> 
> 2. set its version to "1.3"
> 
> 3. `brew install --cask captin` and verify that v1.3 is installed
> ```
> $ mdls -name kMDItemVersion /Applications/Captin.app
> kMDItemVersion = "1.3"
> ```
> 
> 4. revert changes to cask file so `brew info --cask captin` and `brew outdated --cask captin` shows v1.3.1 as the latest, then upgrade
> ```
> $ brew upgrade --cask --greedy captin
> ==> Upgrading 1 outdated package:
> captin 1.3 -> 1.3.1
> ==> Upgrading captin
> ==> Downloading https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cool8jay/public/master/captin/Captin.zip
> Already downloaded: /Users/eric/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/39266fc3264702ef6586dbeab1060e2a56b6e2d04cab21a136446e5c16446068--Captin.zip
> Warning: Cannot verify integrity of '39266fc3264702ef6586dbeab1060e2a56b6e2d04cab21a136446e5c16446068--Captin.zip'.
> No checksum was provided.
> For your reference, the checksum is:
>   sha256 "0240b09755d7b4d77c3a30b4dab780c3059be3e348b71b58899a5ee015ecf8c1"
> ==> Backing App 'Captin.app' up to '/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/captin/1.3/Captin.app'
> ==> Removing App '/Applications/Captin.app'
> ==> Moving App 'Captin.app' to '/Applications/Captin.app'
> ==> Purging files for version 1.3 of Cask captin
> 🍺  captin was successfully upgraded!
> 
> $ mdls -name kMDItemVersion /Applications/Captin.app
> kMDItemVersion = "1.3"
> ```
> 
> The hash in the cached pathname is just the [SHA256 of the source URL](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/3b52a460593fb3f36e5b5fa4bb541ccbb84a4b79/Library/Homebrew/download_strategy.rb#L290), so as long as the URL doesn't change, the cached pathname won't either. The only way for `download_strategy.rb` to know not to use the cache is by checking other metadata like its modification date (see above). One possible approach is to check if the Content-Length matches the cached file size, or to stuff the ETag of a downloaded file into e.g. an extended attribute and later check if it matches, although this assumes the source server is handling those properly.
> 
> ```
> $ curl -I https://www.roboform.com/dist/roboform-mac-v9.dmg
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
> Accept-Ranges: bytes
> Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, must-revalidate
> Content-Length: 45797138
> Content-Type: application/octet-stream
> ETag: "12CFBA0200000000B467CB67"
> reason: OK
> server: SibHtmlServer
> server-id: -
> ```
> 
> And yes, this is one of the [two hard things in computer science](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/TwoHardThings.html). 

 _Originally posted by @EricFromCanada in [#204166](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/issues/204166#issuecomment-2711876875)_

### Description of issue

The roboform cask (https://www.roboform.com/dist/roboform-mac-v9.dmg) uses an unversioned URL, causing Homebrew to reuse an outdated cached file during `brew upgrade --greedy`. This results in a “successful upgrade” message without installing the latest version from the vendor. Specifically, my installed version remains stuck at 9.6.4 due to a cached file, even though Homebrew reports upgrading from 9.6.5 to 9.6.6.

**NB** This is closely related to the verification point above, that _"I made doubly sure this is not a [checksum does not match / SHA256 mismatch](https://docs.brew.sh/Common-Issues#cask---checksum-does-not-match) error (do not open an issue before trying to open a PR to fix first)."_ However I can't fix this with a PR. The checksum in the formula is correct. It's the caching behaviour that is the problem. Last year I opened https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/issues/18630, where I proposed disabling caching for unversioned URLs in casks. That issue was closed as “not planned,” and I was asked by maintainers to open a formula-specific issue here instead. The roboform cask exemplifies the problem: its unversioned URL and lack of checksum lead to outdated cached files breaking upgrades. I contacted RoboForm about using versioned URLs; their response was, “We’ll forward it to the developers, but it may not be implemented.”
I have attempted a fix in this PR: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/pull/204165


**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Install roboform with `brew install --cask roboform`.
2. Wait for RoboForm to update the file at the unversioned URL.
3. Run `brew upgrade --cask roboform --greedy`.
4. Check the installed version vs. the latest on RoboForm’s site.
NOTE: Because waiting for a new version of Roboform is impractical or annoying, I have tried to attached the cached file so that you can use it. Unfortunately it is 44MB, so I can't. I suspect that a dummy file would do. But if you do want the actual one, tell me how you would like me to deliver it.

**Cached File**
```
❰anthonyholland❙~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads❱✘≻ ls -hl | grep robo
-rw-r--r--@ 1 anthonyholland  staff    44M  9 Dec 12:53 349a2b57a312c7d520b6fd0620596d72707681457e050a50badd706914674642--roboform-mac-v9.dmg
❰anthonyholland❙~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads❱✔≻ 
```

**Expected Behaviour**
Homebrew fetches and installs the latest version (e.g., 9.6.6 or newer).

**Actual Behaviour**
Homebrew reuses the cached file, reinstalls the same version (9.6.4 in my case), and claims success. Output from March 6, 2025:

```
==> Upgrading 2 outdated packages:
cursor 0.45.17,7c00f62dd81412c8defe2b64b4d32d06e0a7e727 -> 0.46.9,3395357a4ee2975d5d03595e7607ee84e3db0f2c
roboform 9.6.5 -> 9.6.6

Already downloaded: /Users/anthonyholland/Library/Caches/Homebrew/downloads/349a2b57a312c7d520b6fd0620596d72707681457e050a50badd706914674642--roboform-mac-v9.dmg
Warning: Cannot verify integrity of '349a2b57a312c7d520b6fd0620596d72707681457e050a50badd706914674642--roboform-mac-v9.dmg'.
No checksum was provided.
For your reference, the checksum is:
  sha256 "9fbac05a13e3e93a27a5bb4325d057cee199e60976d60c2c8f7dbb

### Description of issue

Hi folks - opening this issue because I wasn't sure if this made sense as a discussion topic given the security alert sent by Obsidian. 

Users of Obsidian that have used in-app upgrades from a previous version to Obsidian v1.8.4 (my full version prior to reinstall: v1.4.16) are receiving an in-application notification from Obsidian that they need to fully reinstall the application in order to receive important security updates to Obsidian. Performing a `brew upgrade --cask` does not perform this removal as the Cask contains the `auto_updates` stanza. Users can easily perform this update as required by performing a `brew upgrade --cask obsidian --force` to force re-downloading and installing Obsidian, however it is my opinion that due to the nature of the security update, the Cask should be modified to perform the update process for users for this version. 

I'm not aware if there are mechanisms with Cask formulae to flag users as "normally this autoupdates, but if this latest version according to Homebrew is equal to or newer than the existing version, then perform a full upgrade". If so, I believe this is an appropriate time for this. Barring that, publishing an update to the cask temporarily setting the `auto_updates` stanza and/or adding a `caveats` stanza informing users on how to perform the forced upgrade procedure for this version should be provided.

payload.author: geldot
payload.body:
The `clickhouse` formula installs the `clickhouse` binary distributed by Clickhouse. However, the shipped binary is a self-executing decompressor that overwrites itself. Once overwritten, the binary triggers Mac OS security errors. If you override the errors via Settings, the permissions get reset when the package is updated, and you have to do it all over again.

Possible solution to self-extract the binary before installation (untested, unsure if it'll work):

```
  postflight do
    set_permissions "#{staged_path}/clickhouse-macos#{arch}", "0755"
    system_command "#{staged_path}/clickhouse-macos#{arch}",
                   args: ["--version"],
                   sudo: false
  end
```

Alternatively, ask Clickhouse to ship a non-self-extracting binary:

https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/75921
payload.title: Self-extracting executable in clickhouse cask triggers permission errors
